title: Excel: Copilot Agent Mode (Edit with Copilot) for Microsoft 365 users without a Copilot licence
summary: The briefing passes: its controls and licensing statements are supported, and it explicitly reports Microsoft's conflicting entitlement descriptions. One minor clarification is needed because Microsoft's privacy documentation excludes Anthropic models from the EU Data Boundary.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.

claims.quote: When you're updating budgets, creating financial models, or analyzing data, Agent Mode uses Excel's most powerful tools like tables, charts, PivotTables, and formulas to help you get the job done.

claims.quote: Edit with Copilot in Excel to enhance your productivity (formerly Agent Mode)

claims.claim: Users describe requests in chat and Copilot edits the workbook directly.

claims.claim: The March 10, 2026 release notes describe a new option to edit Excel workbooks through chat.
claims.quote:
March 10, 2026
Updates released between February 24, 2026, March 10, 2026
What changed: A new option is available in Copilot in Excel that enables you to edit your workbook through chat.

claims.claim: At that release, the documented entry experience displayed a Let's edit together welcome message.
claims.quote: Open Copilot chat in Excel and see "Let's edit together" welcome message.

claims.claim: The historical instructions say to select Edit with Copilot from the tools menu if the welcome message is absent.
claims.quote: If you don't see the message, then go to the tools menu and select "Edit with Copilot".

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: The current guide says to open Copilot using its icon in Excel's lower-right corner.
claims.quote: Select the Copilot icon in the lower-right corner of Excel.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout and At rollout
claims.claim: Copilot in Excel opens in edit mode by default.
claims.quote: By default, Copilot in Excel opens in edit mode. In editing mode, Copilot in Excel can edit your workbook directly based on your requests.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap description nor the release notes entry describes an administrator step required before using this capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Excel Edit with Copilot Agent Mode enable administrator prerequisite tenant switch. Read roadmap description, March 10 Excel release-note entry, Excel getting-started guide and FAQ; no feature-specific admin enablement step in the roadmap or entry.

claims.claim: The September 23, 2026 release notes describe response navigation links and Copilot attribution in Show Changes.
claims.quote:
September 23, 2026
Updates released between August 26, 2026, and September 22, 2026.
Navigate to your workbook changes directly from the Copilot chat pane response
See Copilot usage in show changes pane

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Copilot responses link users to the sheets, tables, ranges and objects changed in the workbook.
claims.quote: In Copilot in Excel, the response contains links to highlight where changes are made in your workbook. Navigate directly to new sheets, tables, ranges, and objects like charts and shapes.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Excel's Show Changes pane displays Copilot attribution cards for users reviewing AI-generated changes.
claims.quote: Open an Excel workbook with Copilot edits. Select Review tab, then click Show Changes. Look for Copilot attribution cards indicating AI-generated changes.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The FAQ states that Basic users without the Copilot add-on have standard access to Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: M365 Copilot (Basic) indicates that a user does not have the Microsoft Copilot add-on license but does have standard access to Copilot in Excel.

claims.claim: The included entitlement model is supported by the FAQ's standard access without the add-on, with the service-description disagreement retained in the notes.
claims.quote: M365 Copilot (Basic) indicates that a user does not have the Microsoft Copilot add-on license but does have standard access to Copilot in Excel.

claims.claim: Copilot can generate and apply formulas across workbook sheets.
claims.quote: Generate data and formulas: Generate data based on your prompts, perform calculations and apply formulas across multiple sheets, and summarize data.

claims.claim: Copilot can add worksheets.
claims.quote: Edit worksheets: Add, rename, and delete worksheets

claims.claim: Copilot's saved workbook changes can reach other people using a shared workbook.
claims.quote: When you save Copilot changes to your workbook, anyone with access to the file can see those changes, including people in a coauthoring session.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The capability is user-opt-in: users initiate workbook changes by submitting requests to Copilot.
claims.quote: After you submit a prompt, Copilot analyzes your task and creates a step-by-step plan. In editing mode, it works directly in your workbook to carry out that plan

claims.claim: Group Policy Management locates Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content under User Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Office 2016 > Privacy > Trust Center.
claims.quote: If you’re using the Group Policy Management tool, all these policy settings are located under User Configuration\Policies\Administrative Templates\Microsoft Office 2016\Privacy\Trust Center.

claims.claim: UserContentDisabled set to 2 under HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy disables the content-analyzing connected-experiences policy.
claims.quote:
Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content | UserContentDisabled | 1=Enabled 2=Disabled
[HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Policies\Microsoft\office\16.0\common\privacy]

claims.claim: The connected-experiences policy is also configurable through Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: These policy settings can be implemented by using either Group Policy or Cloud Policy.

claims.where: controls[0].governs and note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Turning off content-analyzing connected experiences removes Copilot features, including the Excel editing capability, across Excel, OneNote, Outlook, PowerPoint and Word on devices.
claims.quote: If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps: Excel; OneNote; Outlook; PowerPoint; Word.

claims.claim: Content-analyzing connected experiences remain available when their policy is unconfigured.
claims.quote: If you don’t configure this policy setting, these connected experiences will be available to your users.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The same content-analyzing connected-experiences policy also governs features such as PowerPoint Designer and Translator.
claims.quote:
For example, PowerPoint Designer or Translator.
You can use the Allow the use of connected experiences in Office that analyze content policy setting to control whether these types of connected experiences are available to your users.

claims.claim: Microsoft states the connected-experiences effect for current app versions on Windows, Mac, iOS and Android devices.
claims.quote: This applies to when you're running the most current version of these apps on Windows, Mac, iOS, or Android devices.

claims.claim: Office for Mac has a separate privacy-control documentation page from the Windows Group Policy route.
claims.quote: For information on how to manage privacy controls for Office for Mac, see Use preferences to manage privacy controls for Office for Mac.

claims.claim: Office for the web has its own privacy-control documentation page.
claims.quote: For information about privacy controls for Office for the web applications, see Use policy settings to manage privacy controls for Office for the web applications.

claims.claim: User licence assignment is managed in Microsoft 365 admin center at Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph PowerShell assigns a user licence with Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @().
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: removing a licence
claims.claim: The briefing presents licence assignment or removal as governing entitlement only under the service description's requirement, not as a confirmed way to deny the roadmap's unlicensed access.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) features: A Microsoft 365 Copilot license is required to access this feature.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and controls[2].api; Why it matters; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft documents no independent tenant UI or automation switch for Agent Mode or Edit with Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Excel Agent Mode Edit with Copilot admin disable independent policy Graph fair use limits; Excel Agent Mode disable Graph admin; Excel Edit with Copilot admin turn off. Opened Excel FAQ, manage-copilot-chat and privacy controls; FAQ says it can't be turned off independently.

claims.claim: The Excel FAQ identifies Copilot in Excel as a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool.
claims.quote: Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool

claims.claim: The Excel FAQ says Copilot in Excel cannot be turned off independently.
claims.quote: Copilot in Excel is a Microsoft Copilot Chat tool and can't be turned off independently.

claims.claim: The Excel FAQ says all administrator settings controlling access to Microsoft Copilot Chat apply to Copilot in Excel.
claims.quote: All admin settings for controlling access to Microsoft Copilot Chat apply.

claims.claim: Microsoft's overview says Basic users without the add-on cannot use organisational data through Microsoft Graph when interacting with Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic) and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) can't use organizational data via Microsoft Graph when interacting with Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Users without the add-on can provide organisational content by uploading it or working with open content.
claims.quote: You must upload the content with your prompt, work with open content (Teams and Outlook), or use a pay-as-you-go agent that has access to organizational data.

claims.claim: Prompts and responses are covered by Enterprise Data Protection when users sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts.
claims.quote: Copilot Chat (Basic), Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic), and Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium) are protected by Enterprise Data Protection (EDP) when you sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts.

claims.claim: Microsoft's overview says EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary.
claims.quote: EU traffic stays within the EU Data Boundary, while worldwide traffic can be sent to the EU and other countries or regions for LLM processing.
claims.fix: Retain the attribution to the overview, but add: 'Microsoft's privacy page qualifies this: models provided by Anthropic as a subprocessor are currently excluded from the EU Data Boundary.' Link https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy. The Excel FAQ confirms that Copilot in Excel supports Anthropic models.

claims.claim: Microsoft's overview says worldwide traffic may be sent to other countries or regions for processing.
claims.quote: worldwide traffic can be sent to the EU and other countries or regions for LLM processing.

claims.claim: No new sign-in mechanism is described for the Excel editing capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Excel Agent Mode sign-in permissions connector; Excel Edit with Copilot Agent Mode enable administrator prerequisite tenant switch. Opened March release-note entry, Excel guide and FAQ; no feature-specific new sign-in mechanism described.

claims.claim: No new permission is described for the Excel editing capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Excel Agent Mode sign-in permissions connector. Opened March Excel release-note entry, Excel getting-started guide and FAQ; no new permission grant described for this editing capability.

claims.claim: No new connector is described for the Excel editing capability.
claims.quote: Searched: Excel Agent Mode sign-in permissions connector. Opened March Excel release-note entry, Excel getting-started guide and FAQ; no new connector described as a prerequisite for this editing capability.

claims.claim: The separate Excel Agent in the Microsoft Copilot app requires a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Word, Excel, and PowerPoint Agents are premium capabilities available only to users with a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Microsoft's overview says some features for users without the add-on are subject to fair use limits.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot (Basic) refers to users without the Copilot add-on license, but who have access to Copilot capabilities inside apps (for example, Word or Excel). It doesn't include full chat integration. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: A numeric fair use limit specifically for Agent Mode in Excel is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Excel Edit with Copilot fair use limits; Excel Edit with Copilot Agent Mode fair use numeric limits standard access. Opened Copilot overview, Excel guide, Excel FAQ and Copilot Chat limits page; no feature-specific numeric fair use limit published.

claims.claim: Microsoft's limits page explicitly says it does not publish or share specific numeric limits because service limits can vary.
claims.quote: Because service limits can vary, Microsoft does not publish or share specific numeric limits.

claims.quote: Searched: Excel Edit with Copilot admin turn off. Read the complete Manage Copilot Chat page, including Block users from using Copilot Chat and Remove access to Copilot Chat; no explicit Excel entry. Read Excel FAQ's statement that all Copilot Chat access settings apply.
